edhrecContext.summary: Current EDHREC context shows approximately 3.8K Mazirek decks. Leading tags are +1/+1 Counters, Sacrifice, Aristocrats, and Tokens; the average-deck page reinforces sacrifice outlets, token engines, death-trigger draw, ramp, interaction, and protection. This is context only, not ownership or legality validation.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC popular tags
themeNotes.summary: +1/+1 Counters (392), Sacrifice (292), Aristocrats (209), Tokens (174)

plan.commanderPlan: Create and sacrifice expendable permanents so Mazirek turns each sacrifice into a board-wide +1/+1 counter, then convert the enlarged board into combat damage or aristocrats life loss.
plan.subthemes: Token fodder and death triggers; +1/+1 counters; sacrifice outlets and edict effects; modest recursion and land-sacrifice value.
plan.curveTempo: Run 34 actual lands (16 Forest, 15 Swamp, High Market, Myriad Landscape, and Spawning Bed) with 11 ramp cards, keeping the early curve dependable for a five-mana commander. The list favors one- and two-mana accelerants and token engines, while trimming slower ramp and standalone high-cost cards; the resulting tempo is tuned-casual rather than cEDH.
plan.interaction: Permanent removal, edicts, graveyard hate by combat/value, and flexible protection support a tuned-casual table.
plan.cardAdvantage: Arena, Tracker, Skullclamp, Haruspex, Disciple, Abomination, Rites, Dispute, Village Rites, Life’s Legacy, and Inspiring Call turn expendable bodies or counters into cards.
plan.mana: 34 actual lands: 16 Forest, 15 Swamp, High Market, Myriad Landscape, and Spawning Bed, plus 11 ramp cards (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Golgari Signet, Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Elvish Mystic, Llanowar Elves, Growth Spasm, Kodama's Reach, Rampant Growth, and Sakura-Tribe Elder).
plan.closingPlan: Build wide, grow through Mazirek/Hardened Scales/Corpsejack Menace, then finish with Beastmaster Ascension, Pathbreaker Ibex, token armies, or Blood Artist/Zulaport Cutthroat.
plan.coherence: The remix removes slow, conditional, and off-plan cards, adds redundant fodder/outlets/draw, and gives the list a clearer tuned-casual curve without making a cEDH claim.

swaps.reason: Replace a low-synergy punishment body with death-trigger card advantage.
Replace slow land ramp with efficient two-mana fixing.
Keep the edict effect while lowering the curve.
Upgrade one-shot filtering to repeatable token-based draw.
Replace clunky equipment with a scalable death-trigger resource engine.
Trade a seven-mana theft effect for immediate sacrifice interaction.
Add flexible instant-speed permanent interaction.
Replace slow tutoring with protection and counter-based draw.
Replace an off-plan beater with an aristocrats finisher.
Replace Deadly Tempest with Fleshbag Marauder: Add a repeatable edict creature that turns its own body into Mazirek counter value.
Replace Death's Presence with Grave Titan: Add a threat that continuously produces sacrifice fodder while closing through a wide board.
Replace Evolving Wilds with Nest Invader: Add a two-body package whose Spawn token supports ramp, sacrifice outlets, and Mazirek triggers.
Replace Fertile Imagination with Pawn of Ulamog: Add a death-trigger token engine that converts creature sacrifices into more fodder.
Replace Font of Fertility with Perilous Forays: Add a sacrifice outlet that turns expendable creatures into land-ramp and counters value.
Replace Foundry of the Consuls with Phyrexian Plaguelord: Add a sacrifice-enabled removal engine that doubles as a way to grow Mazirek.
Replace Ghost Quarter with Sylvan Safekeeper: Add protection that uses expendable lands to preserve the board and trigger Mazirek.
Replace Golgari Cluestone with To the Slaughter: Add flexible instant-speed interaction that supports the plan against creatures and planeswalkers.
Replace Horizon Spellbomb with Phyrexian Altar: Add a free sacrifice outlet that converts expendable creatures into colored mana and Mazirek triggers.
Replace Jund Panorama with Blood Artist: Add an aristocrats payoff that turns each creature death into life loss and life gain.

edhrecContext.summary: EDHREC currently highlights Chaos, Sacrifice, Primal Surge, and Ramp tags. Its Vaevictis recommendations include Rhythm of the Wild, Lightning Greaves, Aid from the Cowl, Swiftfoot Boots, Etali, Haunted Crossroads, Solemn Simulacrum, Mazirek, Wood Elves, Farhaven Elf, It That Betrays, and Overseer of the Damned. The EDHREC article emphasizes ramp, haste, top-deck manipulation, and permanent-heavy construction.

themeNotes.title: Power-level context
themeNotes.summary: Used as recommendation context for tuned casual, not as a legality or ownership check.

plan.commanderPlan: Attack with Vaevictis to sacrifice expendable permanents and cheat permanents from the top of the library; haste and protection make the attack trigger reliable.
plan.curveTempo: Cheap mana creatures and rocks accelerate Vaevictis; the top end is reserved for engines and finishers.
plan.interaction: Decree of Pain, Ob Nixilis, Overseer, Trial of Ambition, Poison-Tip Archer, and Vaevictis provide removal; Greaves, Boots, Rhythm, Fires, Fervor, and Whip protect tempo.
plan.cardAdvantage: Elemental Bond, Catacomb Sifter, Tireless Tracker, Satyr Wayfinder, Yavimaya Elder, Ulvenwald Mysteries, and top-deck selection sustain material.
plan.mana: 29 Scryfall-identified land cards plus substantial permanent ramp. The final card color-identity and Commander-legality checks passed; the number and distribution of colored sources remain a proposed shell and have not been playtested.
plan.closingPlan: Repeated Vaevictis triggers, death-drain, landfall armies, Etali/It That Betrays value, and combat finishers. Tuned casual, not cEDH.
plan.coherence: Cuts narrow or low-impact cards, adds explicit sacrifice payoffs, haste/top-deck support, interaction, and a complete land base while preserving the strongest public parent permanents.

edhrecContext.summary: Current EDHREC aggregate context lists Minotaurs, Discard, Aggro, and Hellbent as prominent Neheb tags. Top recommendations include Kragma Warcaller, Rageblood Shaman, Ragemonger, Felhide Petrifier, Sethron, Deathbellow War Cry, Neheb the Eternal, Glint-Horn Buccaneer, and Fanatic of Mogis. The Minotaurs and self-discard pages also surface Bottomless Pit, Geths Grimoire, discard/value cards, and Rakdos interaction. EDHREC is recommendation context, not legality or power certification.

themeNotes.summary: Current EDHREC aggregate context lists Minotaurs, Discard, Aggro, and Hellbent as prominent Neheb tags. Top recommendations include Kragma Warcaller, Rageblood Shaman, Ragemonger, Felhide Petrifier, Sethron, Deathbellow War Cry, Neheb the Eternal, Glint-Horn Buccaneer, and Fanatic of Mogis. The Minotaurs and self-discard pages also surface Bottomless Pit, Geths Grimoire, discard/value cards, and Rakdos interaction. EDHREC is recommendation context, not legality or power certification.

plan.commanderPlan: Neheb attacks with a low-hand Minotaur board, applying discard pressure and rewarding hellbent combat.
subthemes: Minotaur tribal lords, cost reduction, token production, and tribal draw.
Discard/hellbent engines with Waste Not, Bottomless Pit, Oppression, Pain Magnification, and Words of Waste.
Madness/graveyard value from Anger, Archfiend of Ifnir, Asylum Visitor, Faithless Looting, and Dark Deal.
Combat finishers through Kragma Warcaller, Fanatic of Mogis, Neheb, the Eternal, Mogis, and Deathbellow War Cry.
plan.curveTempo: 37 lands, a two-to-four mana creature start, efficient Rakdos rocks, and fewer clunky high-cost effects.
plan.interaction: Abrade, Bedevil, Chaos Warp, Rakdos Charm, Terminate, Vandalblast, Withering Torment, and discard engines.
plan.cardAdvantage: Asylum Visitor, Greed, Geths Grimoire, Waste Not, Dark Deal, Faithless Looting, Sign in Blood, Read the Bones, and tribal Banner/Horn.
plan.mana: 37 lands plus Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Rakdos Signet, Fellwar Stone, Mind Stone, and Hazorets Monument.
plan.closingPlan: Make Minotaurs evasive, amplify combat, convert damage into mana with Neheb the Eternal, then finish through combat and attrition.
plan.coherence: This is a singleton, 100-card Commander proposal with a clear Minotaur/discard/hellbent identity, real mana, compact interaction, and multiple draw engines; it is tuned casual, not cEDH.

edhrecContext.summary: EDHREC currently aggregates 5,687 Alesha decks. Its visible popular tags emphasize Reanimator (492), Aristocrats (267), Aggro (250), and Combo (155); the child uses the first two as its primary tuned-casual identity and explicitly avoids a cEDH claim. EDHREC top-card context includes Faithless Looting, Karmic Guide, Swords to Plowshares, Buried Alive, Viscera Seer, Welcoming Vampire, Mentor of the Meek, and Reveillark.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC popular tags
themeNotes.summary: Reanimator (492), Aristocrats (267), Aggro (250), Combo (155)

plan.commanderPlan: Attack with Alesha, pay {W/B}{W/B}, and recur power-2-or-less creatures tapped and attacking; stock the graveyard with looting/tutors, then convert repeated ETBs and deaths into cards, mana, removal, and damage.

subthemes.name: aristocrats and sacrifice
subthemes.role: Free sacrifice outlets turn recursive bodies into selection and life-loss.

subthemes.name: graveyard setup and recursion
subthemes.role: Put targets in the graveyard and reuse them without relying on a single combo.

subthemes.name: token/artifact value
subthemes.role: Tokens and disposable artifacts provide bodies, mana, and cards.

plan.curveTempo: The child lowers the number of slow five-to-seven-mana standalone artifacts and taplands, adds one- to three-mana setup, outlets, rocks, and removal, and keeps a few high-impact four-to-six-mana recursion/payoff cards. Alesha is the midgame pivot, not a turn-three race requirement.
plan.interaction: A mix of Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Mortify, Anguished Unmaking, Generous Gift, Wear // Tear, Rakdos Charm, Terminate, Tragic Slip, Nekrataal, Fiend Hunter, Leonin Relic-Warder, and a flexible Blasphemous Act/Fell the Mighty package.
plan.cardAdvantage: Faithless Looting, Mentor of the Meek, Welcoming Vampire, Skullclamp, Night's Whisper, Outpost Siege, Daretti, Solemn Simulacrum, Village Rites, Plumb the Forbidden, and repeated ETB/death recursion.
plan.mana: 34 lands plus Sol Ring, six two-mana rocks, Ashnod's Altar, Burnished Hart, and Talisman of Indulgence; the mana base is intentionally practical rather than luxury-heavy.
plan.closingPlan: Build a disposable board, recur value creatures through Alesha/Karmic Guide/Reveillark, then finish with Blood Artist/Zulaport Cutthroat, Goblin Bombardment, Marionette Master, Cathars' Crusade combat, or a Living Death swing. No cEDH fast-combo claim is made.
plan.coherence: The parent pool mixes modular artifacts, token makers, sacrifice pieces, and reanimation without enough density or fixing. This child trims isolated modular/defensive cards, improves early mana and colored sources, and concentrates creatures that are useful both in the graveyard and when re-entering the battlefield.

plan.commanderPlan: Use Ruric Thar as the top-end pressure engine: attack with a dense creature board while making opposing noncreature spells costly. The commander assignment is inferred, so the child remains hypothetical and unplayed; separate Scryfall checks confirmed commander eligibility, color identity, and Commander legality.
plan.subthemes: Werewolf/tribal package supplies board presence and transformation payoffs; creature-based ramp accelerates into Ruric Thar and finishers; combat engines and anthems convert wide boards into lethal attacks; a compact interaction/protection suite preserves pressure.
plan.curveTempo: The list is creature-forward with early mana creatures and two-mana-to-four-mana tribal bodies, then five-plus-mana engines and finishers. Fires of Yavimaya improves post-ramp tempo; the build intentionally avoids becoming a spell-dense control deck.
plan.interaction: Hull Breach, Moonlight Hunt, Moonmist, Reclamation Sage, Ulvenwald Tracker, and Decimate answer key permanents or creatures while respecting the commander plan; combat-based answers are preferred where possible.
plan.cardAdvantage: Duskwatch Recruiter, Hermit of the Natterknolls, Sage of Ancient Lore, Primordial Sage, Vanquisher’s Banner, and Eternal Witness provide creature- or tribe-linked selection, draw, and recursion.
plan.mana: The list has exactly 36 lands plus the nonland mana sources: Cryptolith Rite, Citanul Hierophants, Urza’s Incubator, Whisperer of the Wilds, Wood Elves, Zendikar Resurgent, Quirion Elves, and Firewild Borderpost.
plan.closingPlan: Build a wide Werewolf/creature board, protect the key attack with tribal/pump effects, then close through Beastmaster Ascension, Thunderfoot Baloth, Siege Behemoth, Wolfir Silverheart, Warstorm Surge, and commander damage.
plan.coherence: Compared with the incomplete parent, this child preserves the public creature/tribal identity, moves the inferred commander into the correct zone, and uses exactly five public sideboard cards to reach 100. The additions improve ramp, recursion, interaction, haste/tempo, and a board-wide combat payoff without claiming ownership or importing hidden cards.

plan.commanderPlan: Connect Brago in combat, then blink nonlands after combat to reuse ETB effects, reset Reality Acid, generate artifact/token value, and repeatedly deploy protection or interaction. The child is hypothetical and tuned-casual, not cEDH.
plan.subthemes: Primary blink/ETB value; secondary artifact recursion and token pressure (Blade Splicer, Myr Battlesphere, Mirrorworks, Thopter Spy Network); soft control through Stonehorn Dignitary and Rishadan creatures; limited combat-finisher package.
plan.curveTempo: Prioritize one-to-three-mana setup, ramp, draw, and protection so Brago can begin generating value promptly; retain a few high-impact five-to-seven-mana ETB payoffs as blink targets rather than loading up on disconnected top-end.
plan.interaction: Counterspell and Swords to Plowshares add efficient stack and creature interaction; Grasp of Fate, Reality Acid, Reflector Mage, Tragic Arrogance, and blink effects answer permanents while preserving ETB value.
plan.cardAdvantage: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Ephara, Ichor Wellspring, Mycosynth Wellspring, Thopter Spy Network, and blinkable utility creatures keep cards flowing.
plan.mana: A basic-heavy Azorius base with 36 Scryfall-identified land cards, Command Tower, utility lands, Sol Ring, Knight of the White Orchid, Solemn Simulacrum, and Vedalken Engineer. Color identity and Commander legality passed Scryfall checks; colored-source balance and playability remain untested.
plan.closingPlan: Win through accumulated Brago-triggered value, artifact and golem/thopter bodies, evasive commander damage, and large ETB finishers such as Myr Battlesphere and Scourge of Fleets; no cEDH speed claim is made.
plan.coherence: The changes remove isolated mill, infect, aura, morph, and wheel packages while adding efficient interaction, tutoring, multiplayer draw, and commander protection. This concentrates the parent pool on Brago combat connection plus repeatable ETB/blink value.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC aggregate and theme context
themeNotes.summary: EDHREC currently shows 3,937 Brion decks. Leading tags are Theft (181), Fling (140), Lifegain (107), and Burn (71). Its upgraded aggregate shows 281 decks and overlaps this pool on Captivating Crew, Feldon, Gisela, Gift of Immortality, Stalking Vengeance, Sun Titan, and Zealous Conscripts.

plan.commanderPlan: Cast Brion Stoutarm, temporarily steal opposing creatures, then sacrifice them to Brion or another outlet for player damage and lifegain. Recursive and disposable bodies become reach while Brion stabilizes life totals.
subthemes: Theft package converts Act, Crew, Harness, Mark, Mass Mutiny, Mob Rule, Traitorous Instinct, and Zealous Conscripts into sacrifice fuel.
Sacrifice/fling package uses Ashnod's Altar, Brion, Fling, Goblin Bombardment, Grab the Reins, Heart-Piercer Manticore, and Rupture as outlets.
Recursion/copy package uses Feldon, Flameshadow Conjuring, Mimic Vat, Sun Titan, Twinflame, Gift of Immortality, Goblin Welder, and Treasure Keeper.
Damage/lifegain package uses Gisela, Electropotence, Ogre Battledriver, Serra Avatar, Stalking Vengeance, Well of Lost Dreams, and Brion.
plan.curveTempo: Two- and three-mana ramp, protection, theft, and setup lead into a restrained top end of Gisela, Serra Avatar, Stalking Vengeance, Steel Hellkite, and other payoffs. This is tuned casual, not a cEDH race or deterministic combo build.
plan.interaction: Swords to Plowshares, Condemn, Banishing Light, Aura of Silence, Orim's Thunder, Return to Dust, Steel Hellkite, Ingot Chewer, and Rout answer threats; theft spells are also interaction and fuel.
plan.cardAdvantage: Skullclamp, Well of Lost Dreams, Commander's Sphere, Treasure Keeper, Mimic Vat, Feldon, Sun Titan, and repeatable theft provide cards or material. Heliod's Pilgrim and Taj-Nar Swordsmith tutor narrow package pieces.
plan.mana: The 99 includes 36 Scryfall-identified land cards plus Sol Ring, Boros Signet, Ashnod's Altar, Coldsteel Heart, Mind Stone, Worn Powerstone, Burnished Hart, Knight of the White Orchid, Pilgrim's Eye, Tithe, and Treasonous Ogre. Color identity and Commander legality passed Scryfall checks; colored-source balance and playability remain untested.
plan.closingPlan: Convert stolen high-power creatures or recursive bodies into Brion damage, amplify with Gisela or Electropotence, and finish via repeated fling effects, Stalking Vengeance, Serra Avatar, Savage Beating, or a wide Mob Rule turn.
plan.coherence: The parent already contains the Brion theft/sacrifice shell but is seven cards over target after moving Brion to the command zone. These cuts remove narrow combat, landfall, generic aggro, and slow table-dependent cards without inventing additions, concentrating the existing engine.

themeNotes.title: Aggregate caveat
themeNotes.summary: The source source list was saved as Vintage and lists 105 main copies plus 68 sideboard copies; those counts are preserved as source metadata, not treated as Commander validation.

plan.commanderPlan: Gain life before combat so Licia's generic cost reduction is meaningful, then use her lifelink and once-per-turn five-life payment to grow a protected first-strike threat. Drain payoffs turn the same life movement into reach.
subthemes: Lifegain enablers and repeatable life payment: Soul Warden, Suture Priest, Dega Sanctuary, Gonti's Machinations, Tavern Swindler, Ajani's Pridemate, Sunbond.
Vampire/lifelink pressure: Gifted Aetherborn, Drana's Emissary, Cliffhaven Vampire, Tithe Drinker, Vampire Nighthawk, Vona, Bloodsworn Steward.
Aristocrats and life-loss payoffs: Blood Artist, Falkenrath Noble, Zulaport Cutthroat, Vito, Sanguine Bond, Vizkopa Guildmage, Defiant Bloodlord.
Resilient finishers and alternate pressure: Elenda, Sunscorch Regent, Debt to the Deathless, Approach of the Second Sun, Chandra's Ignition.
plan.curveTempo: Lower the average curve than the 105-card source by removing narrow or redundant effects, add early lifegain bodies and two-mana rocks, and reserve expensive spells for flexible sweepers and closers. Haste is represented by Hammer of Purphoros and protection by Swiftfoot Boots/Boros Charm; Licia should not be exposed without a meaningful protection line when possible.
plan.interaction: Swords to Plowshares, Vendetta, Crackling Doom, Ayli, Vona, Anguished Unmaking, Fell the Mighty, Toxic Deluge, Fumigate, Authority of the Consuls, Kambal, and Withering Boon cover creature, permanent, and go-wide threats without pretending to be cEDH stack control.
plan.cardAdvantage: Phyrexian Arena, Greed, Well of Lost Dreams, Bloodgift Demon, Alhammarret's Archive, Palace Siege, and life-linked engines sustain the hand without claiming fast-combo consistency.
plan.mana: 37 Scryfall-identified land cards plus Sol Ring, Orzhov Signet, Mardu Banner, Commander's Sphere, Pristine Talisman, and Bontu's Monument. Color identity and Commander legality passed Scryfall checks; colored-source balance and playability remain untested.
plan.closingPlan: Convert a large life total into a lethal Licia commander-damage swing, or assemble overlapping drain from Sanguine Bond/Vito/Vizkopa Guildmage/Defiant Bloodlord with Blood Artist-family triggers. Debt to the Deathless, Chandra's Ignition, and Approach of the Second Sun are backup finishes.
plan.coherence: The parent pool was over target and mixed lifegain, generic removal, alternate wins, and unrelated high-cost effects. This child makes lifegain the tempo engine, keeps only the most on-plan parent cards, promotes sideboard cards that directly reinforce the plan, and adds only two targeted staples. It is a tuned-casual recommendation, not a cEDH claim.

themeNotes.summary: The EDH Benchwarmers article explicitly described sacrifice outlets, +1/+1 counter sources, recursion, theft effects, and card draw as the functional Marchesa engine, naming Ashnod's Altar, Carrion Feeder, Unspeakable Symbol, Dragon Blood, Simic Fluxmage, Rhystic Study, and threaten effects.

plan.commanderPlan: Marchesa grants dethrone and returns creatures that die with +1/+1 counters. The child builds around stealing or deploying expendable creatures, attacking to place counters, then sacrificing them for value before they return at end step.
plan.subthemes: The core package is sacrifice outlets (Carrion Feeder, Bloodflow Connoisseur, Goblin Bombardment, Altar of Dementia), counter enablers (Unspeakable Symbol, Simic Fluxmage, Volt Charge, Sage of Fables), recursion/persist (Marchesa, Phyrexian Reclamation, Reanimate, Puppeteer Clique, Victimize), and threaten effects (Mark of Mutiny, Harness by Force, Act of Aggression).
plan.curveTempo: The child removes several tapped lands and expensive, one-shot creatures, adds two-mana rocks and cheap selection, and keeps a midrange curve that can deploy an outlet or protection spell before Marchesa.
plan.interaction: The list has spot removal, edicts, a flexible bounce reset, graveyard hate via Bojuka Bog, and a modest stack package (Counterspell, Arcane Denial, Swan Song) without becoming cEDH.
plan.cardAdvantage: Rhystic Study, Skullclamp, Grim Haruspex, Dark Prophecy, Blood Scrivener, River Kelpie, Disciple of Bolas, and Phyrexian Rager convert recurring deaths into cards.
plan.mana: Exactly 37 lands and 10 ramp cards. The mana upgrades add Dimir Signet, Rakdos Signet, Mind Stone, Bloodfell Caves, High Market, and Exotic Orchard while reducing slow fixing.
plan.closingPlan: Repeated death triggers and Flayer of the Hatebound/Deathbringer Thoctar drain life totals; stolen creatures become sacrifice fuel, while Falkenrath Aristocrat, Exava, and recursive boards close through combat.
plan.coherence: The public parent mixes many isolated combat tricks, tapped lands, and expensive payoffs. This revision concentrates slots on the actual Marchesa loop—countered creatures, free outlets, theft, recursion, draw, and protection—so more opening hands contain a functional engine and more deaths generate value.

themeNotes.summary: The EDHREC Commander 2020 Ruthless Regiment article explicitly describes Humans as the tribe and identifies Sigarda as the most popular Human commander in its visible discussion, while recommending go-wide Human support such as Archetype of Courage and discussing token/anthem closing patterns. The…

plan.commanderPlan: Sigarda, Heron's Grace anchors a Selesnya Human board: she protects Humans from opposing spells and creates 1/1 Human tokens when needed, letting a wide creature base become resilient without relying on a single combo piece.
plan.subthemes: Primary package is Humans and go-wide tokens. Champion of the Parish, Thalia's Lieutenant, Mikaeus, Juniper Order Ranger, Sigil Captain, Abzan Battle Priest, and Abzan Falconer form the counter/evasion layer; Cathars' Crusade, Door of Destinies, Vanquisher's Banner, Beastmaster Ascension, and True Conviction are the scalable payoffs. Bygone Bishop, Ulvenwald Mysteries, Tireless Tracker, Mentor of the Meek, Duskwatch Recruiter, Shamanic Revelation, and Yavimaya Elder provide a deliberate value package rather than pure creature-dumping.
plan.curveTempo: The rebuilt list uses a responsible 36-land floor and ten ramp sources so early Human starts can still curve into four-to-six-mana engines. Cheap creatures and two-mana interaction establish the board, mana creatures and land-search spells accelerate the midgame, and Bygone Bishop, Mentor of the Meek, Ulvenwald Mysteries, and Yavimaya Elder prevent the deck from emptying out. The plan is to deploy two or more bodies by the midgame, protect the counter/token board with Sigarda, Mother of Runes, Grand Abolisher, or Inspiring Call, then convert counters and tribal density into evasive combat rather than relying on a fragile equipment package.
plan.interaction: Interaction is distributed across Swords to Plowshares, Condemn, Celestial Flare, Immolating Glare, Dromoka's Command, Prepare // Fight, Krosan Grip, Forsake the Worldly, Fate Forgotten, Sundering Growth, Manglehorn, Devout Chaplain, Ulvenwald Tracker, and Tragic Arrogance, with Wrath of God and Fumigate as emergency resets. Grand Abolisher, Mother of Runes, Frontline Medic, Make a Stand, Safe Passage, and Sigarda preserve the board when committing to combat.
plan.cardAdvantage: Mentor of the Meek, Bygone Bishop, Tireless Tracker, Ulvenwald Mysteries, Duskwatch Recruiter, Shamanic Revelation, Yavimaya Elder, Vanquisher's Banner, and Commanders Sphere create repeatable or burst draw. The package is designed to recover from a sweeper while still rewarding a creature-heavy hand.
plan.mana: The rebuilt hypothetical main has exactly 36 actual lands: 13 packet Land-type cards retained plus 23 clearly labeled new basic Plains additions. It has exactly 10 ramp sources: Avacyn's Pilgrim, Commander's Sphere, Cultivate, Explosive Vegetation, Kodama's Reach, Sol Ring, Selesnya Signet, Natural Connection, Whisperer of the Wilds, and Yavimaya Elder; land utility is counted only as land unless its primary role is explicitly ramp.
plan.closingPlan: Build a protected Human/token board, make it evasive with Abzan Falconer, Cavalry Pegasus, Champion of Lambholt, or Riders of Gavony, then end combat through Cathars' Crusade, Beastmaster Ascension, True Conviction, Eldrazi Monument, or a large Increasing Devotion. Tragic Arrogance can reset blockers while preserving the best board piece.
plan.coherence: The revision moves the inferred commander into the correct zone, removes the illegal duplicate, and promotes sideboard cards that directly reinforce Humans, counters, draw, protection, and flexible interaction. It trims no additional parent cards, preserving the Deckbox source shell while making the 100-card Commander structure explicit.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC evidence
themeNotes.summary: The article describes Gisa and Geralf as a committed Zombie-tribal commander whose mill and graveyard access support a gradual, resilient horde; it specifically discusses Unbreathing Horde, Forgotten Creation, Noosegraf Mob, Custodi Lich, Urza's Incubator, and Perpetual Timepiece.

plan.commanderPlan: Mill on entry, then cast one Zombie from the graveyard each turn; sequence self-mill and discard to keep a high-value Zombie available while rebuilding after removal.
plan.subthemes: Zombie tribal lords and token makers provide board presence; self-mill, Buried Alive, and recursion stock the graveyard; Ashnod's Altar, Nantuko Husk, Fleshbag Marauder, and death payoffs turn creatures into value; Skullclamp, Kindred Discovery, and tribal bodies supply sustained cards.
plan.curveTempo: The 37-land base and low-cost Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Dimir Signet, and Urza's Incubator support a mostly midrange curve. Early turns develop mana, a discard/mill outlet, or a cheap Zombie; the deck aims to double-spell in the midgame rather than race.
plan.interaction: Counterspell, Aetherize, Feed the Swarm, Cruel Revival, Fleshbag Marauder, Noxious Ghoul, Withered Wretch, and commander-recursive Zombies cover stack, creature, enchantment, and graveyard interaction.
plan.cardAdvantage: Cryptbreaker, Blood Scrivener, Bident of Thassa, Fact or Fiction, Forbidden Alchemy, Secrets of the Dead, Skullclamp, Kindred Discovery, Vanquisher's Banner, and Vampiric Rites convert the wide board and graveyard into cards.
plan.mana: Exactly 37 lands: 9 Island, 17 Swamp, and 11 nonbasics including Command Tower, Dimir Aqueduct, Dimir Guildgate, Dismal Backwater, Evolving Wilds, Rootwater Depths, Tainted Isle, Underground River, Jwar Isle Refuge, Watery Grave, and Unholy Grotto; five meaningful ramp pieces supplement them.
plan.closingPlan: Build a wide Zombie board, use lords and Zombie Master to make combat decisive, drain with Gray Merchant and Vengeful Dead, or convert recursive bodies through sacrifice outlets and Rooftop Storm.
plan.coherence: The child removes one-off mill, slow seven-to-nine-mana effects, duplicate/inefficient mana pieces, and low-impact combat cards. It adds focused tutoring, recursive Zombies, a lord, card draw, stack/enchantment interaction, graveyard hate, and cleaner mana while preserving the parent's Dimir Zombie-graveyard identity.

themeNotes.title: Queen Marchesa average deck
themeNotes.summary: The visible average list used 36 lands and showed a compact ramp suite with Arcane Signet, Boros/Orzhov/Rakdos Signets, Sol Ring, Fellwar Stone, and three Talismans, plus broad instant interaction and Court/Ghostly Prison/Marchesa’s Decree effects.

themeNotes.title: Challenge the Stats — Queen Marchesa
themeNotes.summary: The article specifically recommends two-mana Signets/Talismans over slower three-mana rocks, calls Royal Assassin an underplayed deterrent, identifies card advantage as neglected, and highlights Orzhov Advokist, Brutal Hordechief, Mob Rule, and token/Assassin support as useful political tools.

themeNotes.title: Legends’ Legacy Precon Queen Marchesa
themeNotes.summary: The precon page exposed a Queen Marchesa upgrade context and land additions such as Akoum Refuge, Takenuma, Eiganjo, Sulfurous Springs, and Clifftop Retreat.

plan.commanderPlan: Cast Queen Marchesa early enough to establish monarch, then make reclaiming it unattractive with deathtouch Assassin pressure, attack taxes, and selective forced combat. Treat monarch as both the draw engine and the table-politics lever.
plan.subthemes: Monarch and Courts supply the central engine; pillow-fort and attack-tax cards protect the crown; goad/forced-combat cards redirect damage; Ophiomancer, token makers, Skullclamp, Zulaport Cutthroat, and Etchings of the Chosen turn disposable bodies into value; Royal Assassin and deathtouch tokens create deterrence.
plan.curveTempo: The parent’s slow and redundant top end is trimmed for a lower curve: ten two-mana ramp pieces, cheap draw, and one-mana interaction let the deck deploy Marchesa around turn three and keep mana open for politics. Sixteen-ish cards remain at five or more mana as finishers or high-impact stabilizers rather than routine setup.
plan.interaction: The list uses efficient exile, catch-all answers, artifact/enchantment removal, sweepers, and combat blowouts. Interaction is intentionally broad rather than cEDH stack-heavy, matching a mature tuned-casual table.
plan.cardAdvantage: Monarch is backed by Skullclamp, Courts, Mangara, Mentor, Painful Truths, Read the Bones, Night’s Whisper, Cut a Deal, and Smothering Tithe so the deck does not depend on retaining the crown every turn.
plan.mana: Exactly 36 lands and 10 ramp artifacts. The mana base adds Command Tower, Clifftop Retreat, Sulfurous Springs, Eiganjo, Takenuma, and Akoum Refuge while keeping the public tri-color lands and a sensible 6 Plains / 4 Mountain / 5 Swamp split. No land is counted as ramp.
plan.closingPlan: Win through accumulated monarch damage, evasive Court/Assassin/token pressure, Adriana or True Conviction combat, Elspeth’s board and emblem, Gisela-enhanced damage, or a late Mob Rule-style swing represented here by Disrupt Decorum plus a developed board.
plan.coherence: Compared with the over-target parent, this child removes duplicate and low-synergy defensive slots, improves colored two-mana acceleration, raises reliable draw density, and concentrates the creature/enchantment package on monarch retention, political combat, and token conversion. It remains interactive and splashy without fast-combo or cEDH construction.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC evidence
themeNotes.summary: The official article describes Adaptive Enchantment as a Bant, defense-oriented enchantment deck and explicitly identifies tension between incremental-value control and Aura aggression; it favors leaning into incremental value.

plan.commanderPlan: Estrid untaps enchanted permanents and creates totem armor Auras, letting the deck reuse enchantment-based ramp, protect key creatures, and generate incremental planeswalker value. Her ultimate remains a late-game refill rather than a combo requirement.
plan.subthemes: Primary package is enchantress draw and cost reduction: Enchantress's Presence, Satyr Enchanter, Tuvasa, Kestia, Eidolon of Blossoms, Sythis, and Setessan Champion. Supporting packages are Aura-based protection/ramp, Estrid/Oath of Teferi planeswalker value, and token payoffs from Ajani's Chosen and Sigil of the Empty Throne.
plan.curveTempo: The list trims isolated six-to-eight-mana threats and low-impact Auras for one- and two-mana enchantment ramp plus four- and five-mana draw engines. It aims to develop mana and a draw engine early, then play one impactful enchantment per turn while holding up interaction.
plan.interaction: Bant Charm, Pongify, Forbid, Soul Snare, Ground Seal, Trygon Predator, and Reclamation Sage cover creatures, graveyards, artifacts, and enchantments. Bear Umbra, Eel Umbra, Flickering Ward, and Archetype of Imagination provide selective protection or evasion.
plan.cardAdvantage: Enchantress-triggered draw is the backbone, backed by Blue Sun's Zenith, Ever-Watching Threshold, Jace's Archivist, Sage's Reverie, Snake Umbra, Attunement, and Estrid's ultimate.
plan.mana: The final main deck has exactly 38 Land-type cards and 11 ramp cards, including Sol Ring, Cultivator's Caravan, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Gift of Paradise, Dawn's Reflection, Weirding Wood, Llanowar Scout, Marwyn, Fertile Ground, Wild Growth, and Overgrowth. The lower land count fits the tuned-casual curve better than the prior 41-land estimate, while the cheap Auras and enchantment ramp improve colored-mana development and remain reusable with Estrid.
plan.closingPlan: Win through accumulated enchantress cards and a wide board of Sigil/Ajani tokens, then convert that board with Archetype of Imagination, Finest Hour, Nylea's Colossus, or a large Aura-backed threat such as Aura Gnarlid or Bruna. This is a board-centric mature casual plan, not a cEDH combo shell.
plan.coherence: The child removes disconnected colorless threats, political Auras, counter-only creatures, and expensive one-shot spells. It promotes the packet's strongest sideboard enchantment engines and adds only Sythis and Setessan Champion as clearly identified new cards, giving Estrid more relevant permanents to untap and more reliable ways to draw into interaction and finishers.

themeNotes.summary: EDHREC Partner Focus — Akiri, Line-Slinger describes Akiri as a first-strike/vigilance artifact-count payoff, highlights artifact-token makers including Myr Battlesphere and Hangarback Walker, identifies Inspiring Statuary as an improvise payoff, and calls out Tamiyo's Journal/Magnifying Glass and…

themeNotes.title: Upgraded package
themeNotes.summary: The current upgraded/tokens page visibly listed Sai, Master Thopterist, Nettlecyst, Cranial Plating, Storm the Vault // Vault of Catlacan, Dispatch, Thopter Spy Network, Skullclamp, Smothering Tithe, Breya, Etherium Shaper, and Boros Charm as top cards; its high-lift list included Whispersilk…

plan.commanderPlan: Deploy the partner pair as complementary engines: Akiri turns a wide artifact board into a vigilant first-strike threat, while Silas converts safe combat damage into artifact recursion. The deck can play a token-heavy midrange game rather than relying on commander damage alone.
plan.subthemes: Thopter/Servo/Myr/Clue production supports Akiri and metalcraft; Efficient Construction, Thopter Spy Network, Sai, Thopter Foundry, Hangarback Walker, Pia and Kiran, and Myr Battlesphere build the board. Cranial Plating, Nettlecyst, Whispersilk Cloak, Shadowspear, and Whirler Rogue provide the pressure/evasion package. Skullclamp, Vedalken Archmage, Esper Sentinel, Thought Monitor, Shimmer Dragon, and The Reality Chip keep the artifact count translating into cards. Reckless Fireweaver, Marionette Master, Mirkwood Bats, Ghirapur Aether Grid, and Alibou turn token production or artifact deaths into reach.
plan.curveTempo: The revised shell lowers the number of isolated five-to-seven-mana spells, adds one- and two-mana setup, 36 lands, and a denser two-to-four-mana artifact/token core. It aims to establish mana and an artifact body early, then deploy engines while holding up efficient interaction.
plan.interaction: Dispatch, Aetherize, Dispeller's Capsule, Ghirapur Aether Grid, Boros Charm, Alibou, and Silas recursion cover creature, artifact/enchantment, combat, and board-protection needs. The plan is interaction-backed board development, not a fast-combo line.
plan.cardAdvantage: Skullclamp, Esper Sentinel, Vedalken Archmage, Thought Monitor, Shimmer Dragon, The Reality Chip, Bygone Bishop, Tamiyo's Journal, Trail of Evidence, and Smothering Tithe provide repeatable or burst draw while naturally rewarding artifacts and tokens.
plan.mana: Exact main-deck land count is 36. The mana base uses five artifact lands plus Treasure Vault, utility lands, and 21 basics (7 Plains, 6 Island, 4 Swamp, 4 Mountain); Commanders Sphere, Cultivator's Caravan, Etherium Sculptor, Foundry Inspector, and Solemn Simulacrum provide additional acceleration. Color requirements should be checked against the final printing choices before play.
plan.closingPlan: Close through a large Akiri attack enabled by Cranial Plating/Nettlecyst and evasion, a wide token swing backed by Jor Kadeen/Chief of the Foundry/Master Trinketeer, or attrition reach from Reckless Fireweaver, Marionette Master, Mirkwood Bats, Ghirapur Aether Grid, and Alibou. Hellkite Tyrant and Sharding Sphinx are resilient top-end threats.
plan.coherence: The parent had only 60 noncommander cards and no lands, with scattered one-off effects. This child preserves the recognizable artifact/token identity and the strongest public pieces, moves the assigned commanders to the command zone, cuts narrow or off-plan spells, and fills the missing 36-land/acceleration, token-engine, draw, protection, and interaction structure without claiming testing or ownership.

plan.commanderPlan: Keep Arahbo in the command zone to provide the eminence pump, then cast it when the board can exploit the combat trigger and trample. Lead with efficient Cats, use the free power boost to make even small attackers matter, and reserve equipment for a compact support package rather than the primary plan.
plan.subthemes: The primary package is Cat typal: Regal Caracal, Arahbo, the First Fang, King of the Pride, Feline Sovereign, Pride Sovereign, Qasali Slingers, and Kutzil build a wide board with lords and tribal utility. A secondary token package uses Brimaz, Kemba, Ocelot Pride, and Skullclamp. Equipment is a supporting package around Hammer of Nazahn, Sigarda's Aid, Swiftfoot Boots, Sword of the Animist, Taj-Nar Swordsmith, and a few combat tools.
plan.curveTempo: The revision removes several seven-mana or high-equip-cost cards and adds one- and two-mana interaction, two-mana rocks, and more early Cats. Thirty-six lands plus Sol Ring, two Signets, Burgeoning, Sword of the Animist, Cultivate, and other ramp lets the deck develop without abandoning a midrange combat posture.
plan.interaction: The deck now covers creatures, artifacts, enchantments, and problematic permanents through Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile, Beast Within, Generous Gift, Qasali Pridemage, Qasali Slingers, Sylvan Reclamation, Dromoka's Command, and Rout. Protection comes from Heroic Intervention, Kutzil, Prowling Serpopard, Kindred Boon, Swiftfoot Boots, and Akroma's Will.
plan.cardAdvantage: Card flow comes from Guardian Project, Welcoming Vampire, Keeper of Fables, Skullclamp, Soul's Majesty, Life's Legacy, Abundance, Alms Collector, and Return of the Wildspeaker. These engines are tied to the creature and token plan instead of relying on isolated high-cost artifacts.
plan.mana: The final main has exactly 36 lands, including 8 Forests and 6 Plains plus the packet's Selesnya duals, utility lands, and tribal lands. Ramp is 10 cards by primary role: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Selesnya Signet, Burgeoning, Cultivate, Mirari's Wake, Sword of the Animist, Traverse the Outlands, Urza's Incubator, and Zendikar Resurgent. Krosan Verge remains a land first, with incidental fixing and land-thinning value.
plan.closingPlan: Win through combat: build a critical mass of Cats and tokens, use Arahbo's eminence and the tribal lords to make attacks large, then finish with Beastmaster Ascension, Akroma's Will, Mirari's Wake, Return of the Wildspeaker's pump mode, or an evasive/equipped attacker such as Skyhunter Skirmisher. Rogue's Passage and trample from Arahbo help close through stalled boards.
plan.coherence: The parent shell already contained a recognizable Selesnya Cat aggro-midrange core, but it mixed that plan with scattered lifegain, landfall, fog, alternate-win, and oversized equipment cards. This child keeps the strongest public Cat, token, ramp, and equipment signals, moves Arahbo to the command zone correctly, raises the land count to a reliable 36, and replaces the least focused slots with efficient draw, protection, interaction, and Cat lords. It is stronger and more consistent without moving into cEDH fast-mana or compact-combo territory.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC evidence
themeNotes.summary: The June 17, 2025 article describes Inalla as a Wizard ETB-copy commander for control, aggro, and combo shells, and explicitly discusses Bloodline Necromancer plus Ashnod's Altar as a multi-card infinite mana/token line.

plan.commanderPlan: Keep Inalla in the command zone to provide eminence copies whenever a nontoken Wizard enters. Cast her when the board and mana make the five-mana investment worthwhile; pay for the copy trigger on high-value ETB Wizards rather than every body.
plan.subthemes: The primary package is Wizard tribal ETB value: Archaeomancer, Aether Channeler, Venser, Dualcaster Mage, Naru Meha, Bloodline Necromancer, and Sea Gate Oracle become stronger with Naban, Harmonic Prodigy, Panharmonicon, Reflections of Littjara, and Archmage of Echoes. Step Through, Vedalken Aethermage, and Spellseeker improve access to the right Wizard or interaction. Ashnod's Altar plus Bloodline Necromancer and Inalla is a multi-card infinite colorless-mana/token line, included as an optional tuned-casual ceiling rather than a cEDH shell.
plan.curveTempo: The child removes several seven-to-nine-mana sorceries and slow conditional rocks, adds two-mana ramp, flash Wizards, Wizard cost reduction, and cheap counters. It can develop a value creature while holding up interaction and uses blink/copy effects to turn one cast into multiple ETB triggers.
plan.interaction: The list has spot removal, bounce, stack interaction, graveyard-aware answers, a reset package, and Cyclonic Rift as a scalable catch-up card. Flash Wizards let interaction double as an Inalla trigger and board presence.
plan.cardAdvantage: Azami, Arcanis, Kindred Discovery, Sea Gate Oracle, Shadowmage Infiltrator, Merchant of Secrets, Corpse Augur, and repeated ETB/blink lines replace the precon's slower raw-draw spells with board-connected advantage.
plan.mana: The final main contains exactly 38 lands and 6 ramp cards: Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Talisman of Creativity, Fellwar Stone, Commander's Sphere, and Darksteel Ingot. The new untapped/fetchable/check lands reduce the original bounce-land and tapland friction while keeping enough basics for a stable three-color curve.
plan.closingPlan: Win through accumulated Wizard tokens and ETB value, a wide combat step supported by Docent of Perfection and Inalla haste copies, or a controlled Ashnod's Altar/Bloodline Necromancer loop that converts repeated ETBs and sacrifice triggers into a board or damage outlet. Cyclonic Rift or Cyclone Summoner can clear the way without requiring a dedicated cEDH package.
plan.coherence: The public parent mixes Wizards, curses, cascade, symmetrical attrition, and expensive sorceries. This revision keeps its recognizable Grixis Wizard identity while concentrating slots on repeatable ETB doubling, flash utility, recursion, draw, efficient interaction, and a smoother mana base. It is more consistent and resilient at tuned-casual tables without presenting itself as cEDH.

Replace Curse of Opulence with Naru Meha, Master Wizard: Flash lord and spell copier that is both a Wizard body and an ETB value engine.
Replace Curse of Verbosity with Harmonic Prodigy: Doubles triggered abilities of Wizards and other relevant shamans, multiplying the central engine.
Replace Decree of Pain with Stonybrook Banneret: Cost reduction lets multiple Wizards and interaction fit in the same turn.
Replace Etherium-Horn Sorcerer with Panharmonicon: Doubles creature and artifact ETB triggers across the copy/recursion shell.
Replace Izzet Chemister with Ghostly Flicker: Instant-speed blink for two Wizards or a Wizard and a value permanent; works with Archaeomancer loops.
Replace Kess, Dissident Mage with Aether Channeler: Flexible Wizard ETB that supplies a token, bounce, or card selection as needed.
Replace Mairsil, the Pretender with Wizard's Retort: Wizard-synergy counterspell that is efficient once the board is developed.
Replace Magus of the Abyss with Step Through: Wizardcycling finds key bodies while remaining a castable card in the late game.
Replace Magus of the Mind with Vedalken Aethermage: Wizardcycling and flash utility make it a flexible tutor-like role without cEDH fast-mana pressure.
Replace Memory Plunder with Venser, Shaper Savant: Flash Wizard that answers a spell or permanent and is excellent with copy effects.
Replace Mercurial Chemister with Ashnod's Altar: Sacrifice outlet and mana engine that turns Inalla copies of Bloodline Necromancer into a powerful but multi-card combo finish.
Replace Mystifying Maze with Reflections of Littjara: Tribal enchantment doubles Wizard creature spells and reinforces the ETB-copy plan.
Replace Nivix Guildmage with Archmage of Echoes: Wizard payoff that creates additional copies of Wizards, increasing both value and board presence.
Replace Opportunity with Cyclone Summoner: Wizard-based reset that clears opposing boards while preserving the tribal engine.
Replace Portal Mage with Kindred Discovery: Wizard tribal card advantage that turns each real or token Wizard into sustained draw.
Replace Serendib Sorcerer with Viscera Seer: Low-cost Wizard-adjacent sacrifice outlet that smooths draws and supports recursion lines.
Replace Shifting Shadow with Spellseeker: Wizard tutor for key interaction and blink spells, improving consistency without a fast-combo shell.
Replace Spelltwine with Cyclonic Rift: Flexible early interaction and a fair late-game reset that opens a closing combat turn.
Replace Taigam, Sidisi's Hand with Riptide Laboratory: Utility land that repeatedly returns Wizards to hand for reuse of ETB effects.
Replace Temple of the False God with Watery Grave: Untapped, fetchable dual improves early access to blue and black.
Replace Unstable Obelisk with Steam Vents: Untapped, fetchable dual improves early access to blue and red.
Replace Worn Powerstone with Blood Crypt: Untapped, fetchable dual improves early access to black and red.
Replace Dimir Aqueduct with Sulfur Falls: Reliable check land that supports the three-color curve.
Replace Dismal Backwater with Drowned Catacomb: Reliable check land that supports the three-color curve.
Replace Izzet Boilerworks with Dragonskull Summit: Reliable check land that supports the three-color curve.
Replace Jwar Isle Refuge with Arcane Signet: Efficient two-mana fixing for all three commander colors.
Replace Rakdos Carnarium with Talisman of Creativity: Two-mana fixing that accelerates the deck while preserving a lower curve.

This child preserves 70 visible parent main-deck copies, cuts 27 visible parent main-deck copies, promotes 2 visible public-sideboard copies, and adds 27 explicitly marked new additions to reach 99 main cards plus 1 commander (100 total). Missing original rows are not reconstructed; the parent remains unchanged.

edhrecContext.summary: The aggregate supports the existing Demon, mono-black mana, life-loss/lifegain, draw, and recursion identity. The child makes the sacrifice package denser so Ob's Demon-token and emblem modes have a coherent bridge to the existing precon cards. EDHREC frequency is guidance, not a claim of ownership or required inclusion.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC popular tags
themeNotes.summary: Demons (32), Lifegain (20), Self-Damage (10), Devotion (9)

plan.commanderPlan: Ob Nixilis is a value commander: use +2 to stabilize life totals, make 5/5 Demon tokens with -2, and use the emblem as a long-game sacrifice-and-draw engine. The child leans into the token mode while making the life loss and sacrifice clauses productive.
plan.curveTempo: The visible parent had many seven-mana effects and several tapped or colorless lands. The child removes the slowest pieces, adds cheap rocks, one- and two-mana draw, and lower-cost removal, while retaining a splashy six-to-eight-mana finish package for tuned-casual games.
plan.interaction: Spot removal covers creatures and enchantments, with Feed the Swarm, Go for the Throat, Snuff Out, Shriekmaw, Nekrataal, Malicious Affliction, Profane Command, and the existing sweepers. Bojuka Bog and Vampire Hexmage provide narrow but useful graveyard and planeswalker interaction.
plan.cardAdvantage: Sign in Blood, Read the Bones, Night's Whisper, Phyrexian Arena, Bloodgift Demon, Disciple of Bolas, Phyrexian Gargantua, Syphon Mind, Skullclamp, Ayara, and the commander emblem turn expendable bodies and life into cards.
plan.mana: The child stays mono-black and Swamp-heavy. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Charcoal Diamond, Mind Stone, Commander's Sphere, Wayfarer's Bauble, Burnished Hart, Jet Medallion, Crypt Ghast, Magus, and Nirkana Revenant move the deck from setup to large black-mana turns.
plan.closingPlan: Close through repeated Demon tokens, Grave Titan and Kokusho sacrifice loops, Gray Merchant life swings, aristocrats drain from Zulaport/Bastion/Ayara/Konrad, or a large Profane Command/Drana activation. This is a board-value deck, not a cEDH fast-combo shell.
plan.coherence: The revision trims slow, disconnected mono-black threats and narrow spells, then adds repeatable sacrifice fodder, token engines, drain payoffs, cheap draw, and Swamp-based ramp. Those pieces all reinforce Ob Nixilis’s Demon-token mode and a single midrange value plan, with the aristocrats package and Demon top end providing complementary ways to close.

plan.commanderPlan: Connect Brago in combat, then blink nonlands after combat to reuse ETB draw, removal, bounce, Wellsprings, and protection; Rogue's Passage, evasion auras, and Boots support the connection.

plan.interaction: Counterspell, Cancel, Ojutai's Command, Hindering Light, Dovin's Veto, Render Silent, Swords, Path, Act of Authority, Confiscation Coup, Reality Acid, Reflector Mage, Baral's Expertise, and Kirtar's Wrath cover stack, creature, and permanent interaction.

plan.coherence: Unlike the visible 68-card shell, the child reaches Commander size with a real mana base and concentrates additions on blinkable ETB, protection, interaction, and card flow. children.ownershipStatus: Unknown; not checked against any collection.

This child moves Brago from main to commander, cuts 30 visible original main cards, promotes 5 visible public-sideboard cards, and adds 30 explicit new cards, yielding 99 main plus 1 commander = 100. Missing original rows are not reconstructed, and the parent list is unchanged.

edhrecContext.summary: Current aggregate and theme pages support a blink-first ETB/value plan with a smaller artifact support package. The proposal uses those roles but deliberately avoids cEDH combo concentration.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC popular tags
themeNotes.summary: Blink (1780), Control (513), Combo (432), ETB (224), Tokens (188), Stax (157), Artifacts (108), Flying (64)

plan.commanderPlan: Resolve Brago around turn four, give him a safe combat connection with evasion/protection, then blink selected nonland permanents after damage. The child prioritizes repeatable value over fast infinite-combo lines.
plan.subthemes: ETB blink/value is primary; artifacts are a supporting package through mana rocks, Ichor Wellspring, Panharmonicon, Myr Battlesphere, Spine of Ish Sah, Strionic Resonator, and Conjurer’s Closet; token bodies from Blade Splicer, Reef Worm, and Myr Battlesphere give Brago useful attack steps.
plan.curveTempo: The source shell was top-heavy and had too few efficient mana sources. The child adds Sol Ring, three two-mana rocks plus Fellwar Stone, and six fixing lands while retaining Wayfarer’s Bauble, Mind Stone, Solemn Simulacrum, and Traveler’s Amulet. It aims to develop mana early, deploy value creatures on turns three to five, and hold one-mana or two-mana protection/interaction for Brago’s attack turn.
plan.interaction: A mix of spot removal, stack interaction, permanent answers, graveyard hate, and defensive Ghostly Prison; Lux Cannon is a slow repeatable answer that is acceptable for tuned-casual rather than cEDH.
plan.cardAdvantage: Blinking ETB draw creatures and artifacts turns Brago’s combat trigger into incremental cards; Panharmonicon and Strionic Resonator increase the ceiling without requiring a deterministic combo.
plan.mana: 31 lands plus 11 ramp roles, with 13 basics retained from the visible source and a small Azorius fixing suite. Temple of the False God remains a source-row concession but is balanced by better early colored lands.
plan.closingPlan: Win through accumulated evasive combat, Myr Battlesphere and Blade Splicer bodies, token pressure, and repeated Palace Jailer/Spine/Reflector Mage tempo. Rogue’s Passage, Whirler Rogue, and Brago’s flying help force the key connections.
plan.coherence: The child makes Brago’s combat-triggered blink the primary engine: ETB value and interaction, protection for a safe connection, and artifact/token payoffs all reward the same plan. The artifact package supports the blink engine rather than competing as a separate strategy, while accumulated value feeds evasive commander damage and high-impact ETB finishers.

edhrecContext.summary: Current EDHREC aggregate supports counters/proliferate as the coherent lane; the child uses selected core additions but deliberately remains tuned-casual rather than copying infect or optimized/combo packages.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC popular tags
themeNotes.summary: infect (333), plus_1_plus_1_counters (275), proliferate (157), phyrexians (68)

plan.commanderPlan: Atraxa supplies repeatable end-step proliferate while the deck establishes +1/+1 counters across creatures and selected permanents. The child is a fair four-color midrange shell, not an infect or cEDH combo build.
plan.subthemes: The primary package is +1/+1 counters/proliferate: Hardened Scales, Corpsejack Menace, Cathars' Crusade, Forgotten Ancient, Master Biomancer, Vorel, Evolution Sage, Inexorable Tide, Tekuthal, Brokers Ascendancy, Winding Constrictor, and The Ozolith. Ghave, Reveillark, Custodi Soulbinders, and token/counter creatures supply go-wide material; Fertilid, Cultivate, and Farseek convert counters/land drops into a stable board.
plan.curveTempo: The visible parent has a high six-drop and tapped-land burden and only 86 exported cards. The child keeps its visible identity but adds low-to-mid-cost fixing, ramp, proliferate payoffs, and cheap interaction so turns two through five develop mana and counters before Atraxa and the larger engines take over.
plan.interaction: Disdainful Stroke, Mortify, Putrefy, Languish, Duneblast, Merciless Eviction, Necroplasm, Festercreep, Scavenging Ooze, Swords to Plowshares, Anguished Unmaking, and Counterspell cover creatures, artifacts, enchantments, graveyards, and the stack.
plan.cardAdvantage: Fathom Mage, Bred for the Hunt, Inspiring Call, Tezzeret's Gambit, Treasure Cruise, and proliferate engines turn a wide counter board into cards; Atraxa also rewards surviving to the end step.
plan.mana: The source 37 lands/rocks are retained exactly; the additions are Cultivate and Farseek plus Fertilid, improving four-color access without claiming a rebuilt mana base or ownership.
plan.closingPlan: Win through evasive or unblockable countered creatures from Abzan Falconer, Champion of Lambholt, and Tuskguard Captain, or snowball a wide board with Cathars' Crusade, Kalonian Hydra, Enduring Scalelord, Ghave, and Mirrorweave. Simic Ascendancy is a slower alternate counter win.
plan.coherence: Compared with the visible parent, every new card directly advances counters/proliferate, mana, or efficient protection/interaction. The separate child therefore has a clearer Atraxa-centered plan while preserving the visible public rows and making no claim about missing rows.

plan.commanderPlan: Breya is a four-color artifact creature that enters with two Thopters and converts two sacrificed artifacts into removal, direct damage, or life. The child keeps her in the command zone and builds a steady stream of expendable artifacts rather than treating the visible Vintage list as a finished deck.
plan.subthemes: Primary package: Thopters and artifact tokens. Secondary package: artifact sacrifice, recursion, modular/counter bodies, and artifact ETB/value. Skullclamp, Sai, Thopter Spy Network, Sharding Sphinx, Hangarback Walker, and Thopter Assembly turn fodder into cards or more bodies; Ashnod’s Altar, Breya, Slobad, and Marionette Master turn those bodies into mana, removal, and reach.
plan.curveTempo: The additions supply 34 lands and six low-cost nonland spells, correcting the visible list’s missing mana base. Early turns develop rocks, Wellsprings, Inspector/Engineer, and cheap artifact bodies; midgame deploys Breya and token engines while holding capsule or Breya activation; late game converts a wide board into cards, mana, and damage. It is intentionally slower and more interactive than a cEDH combo list.
plan.interaction: Use Breya’s -4/-4 mode, Ethersworn Adjudicator, Executioner’s/Dispeller’s Capsules, Shrapnel Blast, Confirm Suspicions, Nevinyrral’s Disk, Phyrexian Rebirth, Spine of Ish Sah, and Scourglass to answer creatures, artifacts/enchantments, or problematic boards. Protection is structural: Boots, Forge, Padeem, Slobad, and recursion make sweepers less punishing.
plan.cardAdvantage: Vedalken Archmage, Baleful Strix, Brainstorm, Filigree Familiar, Ichor Wellspring, Thopter Spy Network, Tamiyo’s Journal, Skullclamp, Sai, Daretti, Silas Renn, Beacon of Unrest, and Myr Retriever keep resources flowing. The deck avoids relying on a single draw engine.
plan.mana: Thirty-four lands include basics, five-color fixing, artifact lands, Spire of Industry, Inventors’ Fair, and Darksteel Citadel. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Commander's Sphere, Cultivator’s Caravan, Foundry Inspector, Chief Engineer, Mycosynth Wellspring, and Blinkmoth Urn bridge into the six-to-eight-mana artifact finishers.
plan.closingPlan: Win through a wide Thopter/artifact board backed by Master of Etherium, Tempered Steel, Cranial Plating, Sharding Sphinx, Hellkite Igniter, and Darksteel Juggernaut, or drain/finish with Marionette Master, Underhanded Designs, Reckless Fireweaver, Breya damage, Shrapnel Blast, and Hellkite Tyrant. These are board-dependent, fair casual closers rather than deterministic combo claims.
plan.coherence: Compared with the visible parent, the child supplies the missing mana base, a clear Thopter/token density, cheap card flow, repeatable sacrifice outlets, and a defined interaction suite. It preserves the parent’s artifact-recursion identity while removing the ambiguity created by the Vintage label and 40-card gap; no omitted original rows are invented.

plan.commanderPlan: Brion converts any large or temporarily stolen creature into direct player damage and lifegain. The child keeps the visible Giant tribal shell but gives it the lands needed to cast its top end and the card-flow/protection needed to repeatedly activate Brion.
plan.subthemes: Giant density and cost reduction/payoffs (Stinkdrinker Daredevil, Herald's Horn, Sunrise Sovereign, Borderland Behemoth) support a midrange board; theft effects (Besmirch, Hijack, Mark of Mutiny, Kari Zev's Expertise, Unwilling Recruit, Zealous Conscripts, Insurrection) supply disposable bodies; Brion, Bloodshot Cyclops, Grab the Reins and Might Makes Right turn those bodies into damage; recursion/lifegain (Adarkar Valkyrie, Colfenor's Urn, Sigil of the New Dawn, Well of Lost Dreams) rebuilds and rewards the life swing.
plan.curveTempo: The visible shell is top-heavy, so the explicit completion is land-heavy: 35 lands plus the existing Sol Ring, Everflowing Chalice, Boros Cluestone, Marble Diamond, Hedron Archive, Thran Dynamo, Belbe's Portal, Hazoret's Monument and Stinkdrinker Daredevil. This is a slower tuned-casual midrange plan, not a fast combo race.
plan.interaction: Removal and sweepers come from Besmirch, Blind Obedience, Desolation Giant, Glaring Spotlight, Grab the Reins, Hijack, Kari Zev's Expertise, Limits of Solidarity, Mark of Mutiny, Orim's Thunder, Phyrexian Rebirth, Smoke, Stoneshock Giant, Thundercloud Shaman and Unwilling Recruit; theft doubles as interaction and fling fuel.
plan.cardAdvantage: Skullclamp is the single explicit new nonland addition; existing Commander's Sphere, Heirloom Blade, Herald's Horn, Inheritance, Oracle's Vault, Wandering Graybeard and Well of Lost Dreams provide incremental cards or selection.
plan.mana: 35 lands, including basics and Boros/Giant utility lands, smooth the original 64-card land-light shell. Existing rocks and Giant cost reduction bridge to the six- and seven-mana threats.
plan.closingPlan: Attack with Sunrise Sovereign-pumped Giants, then fling a large body with Brion or Bloodshot Cyclops; theft plus Brion creates burst damage, while Hamletback Goliath, Borderland Behemoth, Moltensteel Dragon, Insurrection and Well of Lost Dreams provide scalable late-game reach.
plan.coherence: Unlike the visible 64-card Vintage list, this child has a complete Commander count, a commander-zone move, and an explicit mana foundation. It does not invent hidden original rows: all nonland visible cards remain, and only named additions are added.

plan.commanderPlan: Brion is the repeatable sacrifice outlet: temporary theft effects take the best opposing creature, then Brion converts its power into direct damage and life while the creature is not returned.
plan.subthemes: Theft/Threaten effects; fling and sacrifice outlets; equipment/haste/protection; token, recursion, lifegain and death-value support.

plan.interaction: Burn Away, Fate Forgotten, Orim's Thunder, Planar Outburst, Solemn Offering, Subterranean Tremors, Blessed Alliance and the theft spells answer permanents or turn opposing creatures into Brion fuel.

plan.mana: 36 visible land copies are retained after the two off-color any-color lands are cut; Sol Ring, Ashnod's Altar, Manalith and Hedron Archive provide acceleration. Colored-source balance is not playtested.
plan.closingPlan: Fling large stolen creatures repeatedly, amplify damage with Brion's lifelink and equipment/creature scaling, then finish through Molten Primordial, Zealous Conscripts, Scourge of Geier Reach, Chandra's Ignition or a large equipped attacker.
plan.coherence: Compared with the visible parent, this child keeps its strongest existing Brion identity, removes the duplicate and two off-color lands, and cuts eight narrow/slow cards without inventing an unverified replacement pool.

plan.commanderPlan: Daretti filters dead cards through discard/draw, sacrifices artifacts to recur key permanents, and can convert a wide artifact board into inevitability.
plan.curveTempo: Tuned-casual midrange: low-cost artifact acceleration, untap value, and tutors establish Daretti engines early, with recursion supporting resilient finishers without cEDH fast mana.
plan.interaction: Mono-red removal and sweepers plus Nevinyrral's Disk, Meteor Golem, and Spine of Ish Sah answer creatures, artifacts, enchantments, and other problematic permanents.
plan.cardAdvantage: Daretti, Faithless Looting, Jalum Tome, Wellspring artifacts, and Combustible Gearhulk turn discard and sacrifice into sustained cards.
plan.mana: 39 lands including 27 Mountains plus artifact acceleration; cost reduction, mana rocks, and tutors support the high-end recursion plan without the prior excess-land density.
plan.closingPlan: Recur Myr Battlesphere, Wurmcoil Engine, Hellkite Tyrant, Steel Hellkite, or Meteor Golem through Daretti, Feldon, Scrap Trawler, and Trash for Treasure, then win through artifact pressure or Daretti's emblem.
plan.coherence: Official complete Built from Scratch source normalized to 99 main cards, with all four visible sideboard cards promoted as additions and ten specific one-for-one tuned-casual upgrades; no hidden source rows reconstructed.

themeNotes.summary: Relevant examples observed on the direct page (not copied as a decklist): Sarkhan's Triumph, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Nature's Lore, Kindred Dominance, and Dragonborn Champion.

plan.commanderPlan: The Ur-Dragon is a best-fit inferred commander, kept visibly hypothetical. Cast large Dragons, leverage cost reduction and attack triggers, then close through Dragon ETB damage, combat pressure, and tribal payoffs.
plan.curveTempo: Midrange ramp into a splashy Dragon top end; the 39-land visible shell balances its many tapped/five-color lands with substantial ramp while supporting the inferred commander’s nine-mana cost.
plan.interaction: Kindred Dominance, Swords to Plowshares, Beast Within, Cyclonic Rift, Earthquake, and Dragonlord Atarka answer permanents and boards; Heroic Intervention and Teferi's Protection protect the Dragon board.
plan.cardAdvantage: Kindred Discovery, Elemental Bond, Temur Ascendancy, Shamanic Revelation, Painful Truths, Dragonborn Champion, and Dragon's Hoard sustain a creature-heavy plan.
plan.mana: The visible 39-land Scryfall land suite is paired with Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Chromatic Lantern, land-ramp spells, and Dragon-specific fixing to support five colors and a nine-mana commander without retaining excess basic-land density.
plan.closingPlan: Dragon Tempest and Terror of the Peaks convert Dragon entries into damage; Miirym, Lathliss, Utvara Hellkite, Scourge of the Throne, and large evasive Dragons close games.
plan.coherence: Hypothetical inferred-commander remix of the complete visible source: 31 public-main cuts become 31 new additions, while the visible Ur-Dragon copy moves to the commander zone; no hidden rows or third-party decklist were reconstructed.

themeNotes.title: Average-deck observation
themeNotes.summary: Current average composition shown is 24 creatures, 9 instants, 13 sorceries, 10 artifacts, 6 enchantments, 1 planeswalker and 36 lands. Representative cards include Averna, Maelstrom Wanderer, Imoti, Shardless Agent, Farseek, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach, Rampant Growth, Lightning Greaves and…

plan.commanderPlan: Yidris rewards connecting in combat: give him evasion/protection, then use cascade on increasingly expensive spells to chain value.
plan.subthemes: Cascade/value creatures; wheels and graveyard/spell recursion; four-color ramp and commander protection; token and high-impact spell finishers.
plan.curveTempo: The parent has 39 lands and many expensive sorceries. This child keeps 39 lands, replacing the narrowest top-end/reset effects with four ramp spells, two cascade creatures and two protection pieces. Tuned casual, not cEDH.
plan.interaction: Chaos Warp, Rakdos Charm, Bituminous Blast, Curtains' Call, Decimate, Evacuation and Volcanic Vision provide removal and sweepers; cuts reduce redundant high-cost resets.
plan.cardAdvantage: Windfall, Wheel of Fate, Whispering Madness, Reforge the Soul, Treasure Cruise, Ancient Excavation, Parting Thoughts, Coiling Oracle and Wall of Blossoms supply draw; Averna, Imoti and Shardless Agent add cascade-linked material.
plan.mana: 39 lands are retained, including the precon basics and multicolor lands. Sol Ring, Fellwar Stone, Rakdos Signet, Simic Signet, Chromatic Lantern, Commander's Sphere, Burgeoning, Far Wanderings, Farseek, Cultivate, Kodama's Reach and Rampant Growth provide casual acceleration and fixing; not playtested.
plan.closingPlan: Attack safely with Yidris, chain cascade through Averna, Imoti, Shardless Agent and Maelstrom Wanderer, then convert wheel/spell volume into a wide board, graveyard recasts or high-impact threats such as Blood Tyrant, Consuming Aberration, Runehorn Hellkite and Spellheart Chimera.
plan.coherence: The child moves the assigned commander, removes ten narrow/slow or high-variance cards, and adds focused cascade bodies, land ramp and protection without reconstructing hidden cards, improving early development and connected Yidris-trigger value while preserving the precon chaos/wheels identity.

themeNotes.title: Average-deck observation
themeNotes.summary: The current average deck emphasizes artifact mana and cost reduction (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Izzet Signet, Mind Stone, Worn Powerstone), token/artifact engines (Myr Battlesphere, Sai, Master Thopterist, Thopter Spy Network, Brudiclad, Retrofitter Foundry), and a denser counter/removal package…

plan.commanderPlan: Saheeli discounts artifact spells and creates thopters; the tuned child turns those bodies into improvise mana, copied value, card draw and a decisive combat or artifact-trigger finish.
plan.subthemes: Artifact tokens and thopters; artifact cost reduction and improvise; artifact-copy/value engines; protection and flexible interaction; go-wide combat plus artifact-entry damage.
plan.curveTempo: Tuned casual, not cEDH: 38 lands and 11 ramp-role cards support Saheeli and six-to-eight-mana artifact threats, while cheap cost reduction and token makers improve early sequencing without fast-mana or deterministic combo.
plan.interaction: Blasphemous Act, Chaos Warp, Duplicant, Into the Roil, Magmaquake, Scrabbling Claws and Vandalblast answer creature boards, permanents or graveyards; Padeem adds resilience.
plan.cardAdvantage: Coveted Jewel, Endless Atlas, Reverse Engineer, Thirst for Knowledge, Thought Monitor and Shimmer Dragon keep cards flowing; Sai and Padeem add artifact-matters value.
plan.mana: The child has 38 lands (27 basic Islands/Mountains plus 11 nonbasics) and 11 ramp-role cards, including Arcane Signet, Inspiring Statuary, Etherium Sculptor, Izzet Signet, Sol Ring, Mind Stone, Prismatic Lens, Worn Powerstone, Magnifying Glass, Hedron Archive and Vessel of Endless Rest.
plan.closingPlan: Build thopter/artifact mass, use Sai, Efficient Construction, Brudiclad, Sharding Sphinx and Whirler Rogue for evasive pressure, then close through Hellkite Igniter, Myr Battlesphere, Reckless Fireweaver triggers, Scuttling Doom Engine, Steel Hellkite or a large Saheeli-powered board.
plan.coherence: The ten swaps replace slow, narrow or off-plan cards with EDHREC-supported Saheeli artifact/token patterns: artifact mana, thopter multiplication, board protection, artifact-density draw, and artifact-entry damage. The result is focused and interactive while remaining tuned casual rather than cEDH.

swaps.reason: Arcane Signet replaces broad bounce with cheap Izzet fixing, helping Saheeli come down early and leaving mana for artifact-token development.
Sai, Master Thopterist turns each noncreature artifact into a Thopter and converts spare artifacts to cards, directly multiplying Saheeli and Brudiclad token value.
Efficient Construction rewards every artifact spell with a Thopter, making Saheeli’s cost-reduction plan translate into a wider artifact-token board.
Inspiring Statuary lets Saheeli’s artifact tokens improvise expensive artifact spells, converting a go-wide board into the mana needed for the deck’s top end.
Padeem protects the deck’s key artifacts and draws from the high artifact count, preserving Saheeli’s token engine against removal while replenishing cards.
Thought Monitor uses the growing artifact count for a low-cost two-card refill and adds another artifact body for Saheeli’s reduction and token synergies.
Shimmer Dragon turns expendable Thopters into repeatable card draw, giving Saheeli’s artifact tokens a resilient value role beyond attacking.
Vandalblast supplies efficient interaction against opposing mana rocks and artifact boards while keeping the deck’s own Saheeli-generated tokens intact.
Reckless Fireweaver converts every artifact, including Saheeli’s tokens, into damage, rewarding repeated token creation without relying on combat.
Mystic Forge lets the artifact-dense deck cast from the top of the library, improving Saheeli-era sequencing and maintaining pressure without a deterministic combo.

plan.commanderPlan: Arahbo supplies an eminence combat boost while in the command zone and a late-game trampling pump ability. The child focuses on attacking with a dense Cat board, then converts wide combat into lethal damage through tribal lords and equipment.
plan.subthemes: Cat typal; Equipment; +1/+1-counter-adjacent combat scaling; token production; creature-based draw and protection.
plan.curveTempo: The original precon is top-heavy and artifact-heavy. Twelve cuts remove slow, narrow, or weakly connected effects; Arcane Signet, Nature's Lore, cheaper Cats, and efficient interaction improve turns two through five without turning the deck into cEDH.
plan.interaction: Swords to Plowshares, Beast Within, Condemn, Wing Shards, Rout, Relic Crush, Crushing Vines, Qasali Pridemage, Qasali Slingers, Leonin Relic-Warder and Aura Shards cover creatures, permanents, and go-wide boards.
plan.cardAdvantage: Guardian Project, Kutzil, Skullclamp, Harmonize, Soul's Majesty, Hunter's Prowess, Staff of Nin replacement via creature draw, and Abundance replacement via a denser creature plan keep cards flowing.
plan.mana: 37 lands are retained, with Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Cultivate, Nature's Lore, Nissa's Pilgrimage, Sword of the Animist, Oreskos Explorer and Traverse the Outlands providing acceleration. The count is intentionally casual and supports Arahbo's five-mana body plus equipment turns; colored-source balance was not playtested.
plan.closingPlan: Build a critical mass of Cats, use Regal Caracal, King of the Pride, Feline Sovereign and Arahbo's eminence to make attacks large, then finish with an equipped trampling attacker, Jazal Goldmane, Mirari's Wake, White Sun's Zenith or a wide-board combat step.
plan.coherence: The child preserves the parent's Cats-and-Equipment identity, moves the official commander to the correct zone, increases early ramp and unconditional interaction, adds tribal lords and creature draw, and trims expensive cards that neither advance Cats nor efficiently protect the plan.

themeNotes.title: EDHREC theme
themeNotes.summary: The filtered Elves aggregate is 245 decks. Its top-card and high-lift observations emphasize Elvish Archdruid, Priest of Titania, Llanowar Elves, Elvish Mystic, Imperious Perfect, Marwyn, Reclamation Sage, Beast Whisperer, Ezuri, Elvish Warmaster, Circle of Dreams Druid, Realmwalker, and…

themeNotes.title: Average-deck observation
themeNotes.summary: The current average deck shown by EDHREC is a 33-land shell with 26 Forests and highlights Arcane Signet, Emerald Medallion, Lifecrafter’s Bestiary, Skullclamp, Sol Ring, Swiftfoot Boots, Vanquisher’s Banner, Nykthos, Wirewood Lodge, Yavimaya, Beast Whisperer, Circle of Dreams Druid, Elvish…

plan.commanderPlan: Freyalise supplies repeatable Elf and Saproling bodies, artifact/enchantment removal, and a planeswalker-based draw mode; the child protects her long enough to convert mana into board presence.
plan.subthemes: Elf typal ramp and tribal payoffs; Freyalise/Saproling tokens; creature-based card advantage; land-and-devotion scaling; overrun-style combat finishes.
plan.curveTempo: The source is battlecruiser-leaning, so the child trims seven-mana removal, slow colorless/storage lands, and narrow artifacts for one- to four-mana elves, a two-mana rock, and efficient draw. It remains tuned casual rather than cEDH.
plan.interaction: Reclamation Sage, Song of the Dryads, Terastodon, Silklash Spider, Elvish Skysweeper, Thornweald Archer, Beast Within, and Freyalise’s removal mode cover artifacts, enchantments, large permanents, and flyers; Heroic Intervention and Boots protect the board.
plan.cardAdvantage: Collective Unconscious, Primordial Sage, Soul of the Harvest, Skullclamp, Elvish Visionary, Masked Admirers, Beast Whisperer, Leaf-Crowned Visionary, and Return of the Wildspeaker keep a wide creature board from running out of cards.
plan.mana: The final main deck has 36 lands, including 25 Forests and 11 nonbasics. Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Emerald Medallion, Moss Diamond, the one-mana elves, Priest of Titania, Farhaven Elf, Wood Elves, Circle of Dreams Druid, Harrow, and Growing Rites accelerate into the five- and six-mana payoffs. Nykthos, Wirewood Lodge, and Yavimaya improve late-game scaling and creature mana without making a cEDH claim.
plan.closingPlan: Make a wide board through Freyalise, Hunting Triad, Sylvan Offering, Wolfbriar Elemental, Imperious Perfect, Lys Alana Huntmaster, and Wren’s Run Packmaster; then use Beastmaster Ascension, Overrun, Overwhelming Stampede, Thunderfoot Baloth, Creeperhulk, or a large Joraga Warcaller to close.
plan.coherence: The visible precon already has a strong elf/token identity. These changes reduce slow colorless mana, expensive low-synergy spells, and narrow artifacts while adding the most relevant connective tissue: more early elf mana, creature-based draw, tribal density, protection, and a small set of high-value mono-green lands. The result has clearer sequencing from mana creatures to Freyalise and tribal engines to a board-wide finish.
